per_event.why: Both X and Y show identical ship movement, banking, and the white targeting cone ahead of the ship.
Single tap shots are fired in X (0.0s, 4.9s) and Y (0.6s, 2.5s), but they appear to miss or only charge shots hit.

In X (0.8s, 3.7s, 5.9s) enemies are destroyed with an explosion. In Y (0.0s, 0.9s, 3.1s, 5.5s) enemies are disarmed (red rings disappear, grey hulls float away, HUD text at 1.0s says 'disarmed, not dead'). Both states are communicated clearly in their respective clips.
Wait gauge fills and releases charge shots with a white arc in both X (0.6s, 1.4s, 2.3s, 3.5s, 5.7s) and Y (0.9s, 1.5s, 3.0s, 5.3s, 6.0s).
Charge shots hitting vs missing (e.g. X at 1.4s misses, 0.8s hits; Y at 1.5s misses, 0.9s hits) are equally clear in both.
Neither clip shows shots bouncing off armor.
No boss is present in either clip.
The player loses a hull point in X at 1.8s and 5.9s, and in Y at 2.1s. Both feature a bright red screen border flash, expanding ring on the ship, and a loud impact sound.
Multi-hits from the wide arc shot occur in X (0.8s) and Y (0.9s, 5.5s) and are similarly readable.

clutter.issue: Scrolling vertical white dashes and yellow/green dots on the floor track add visual noise behind combat compared to the clean blue floor in X.
Disarmed grey enemy hulls stay on the playfield drifting downward, which can momentarily compete with active targets against the busier floor.
Full-screen red damage vignette is very intense and briefly obscures peripheral vision (also happens at 5.9s in X and 2.1s in Y).

overall.why: Clip X has a clean, solid blue floor surface that gives maximum contrast to enemy bullets, red target rings, and the player's white aiming arc. Clip Y adds scrolling lane dashes and colored dots on the floor which slightly reduces contrast and adds background motion noise.
